newsitem.title: USA: CBOT May and July soybeans set contract highs.
newsitem.headline: CBOT May and July soybeans set contract highs.

text.p: CBOT soybeans were higher at midsession and contract highs were notched in the May and July on ideas soybeans were set to rally even further on supply concerns, traders said.
Floor sources cited talk an influential U.S. analytical firm had issued a buy recommendation to its clients, saying this may be the last time to buy soybeans before the market rallies sharply.
The talk bolstered bullish sentiment sparked by Thursday's National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush figure and USDA's export figures, traders said.
NOPA put weekly soybean crushings at roughly 25 million bushels, above expectations for 24.1 million to 24.9 million.

Traders and analysts have said weekly crush and export usage levels need to fall below 32 million bushels to stay in line with USDA projections. Thursday's USDA weekly export tally was roughly 14 million bushels.
The new high for the July contract is $8.96 a bushel, topping the previous high of $8.95 set on Thursday and the highest level since the 1988 drought.
At 1200 CDT, soybeans were up 12 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel with July up 12 at $8.89.
Funds were noted buyers in morning trade. Iowa Grain, Refco Inc and Tenco Inc were all said to be on the buy side, traders said.
